summary.summary_text: ACL Cables manufactures and sells electrical cables and related products in Sri Lanka through its own operations and several subsidiaries/associates (including Kelani Cables PLC and Resus Energy PLC) (Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, Annual Report 2024/25). Group revenue rose from LKR 22.62Bn (FY2021) to LKR 37.49Bn (FY2025), +66% over five years, but not steadily -- it spiked 56% in FY2022, then fell for two straight years before rebounding sharply in FY2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Profitability has been considerably more volatile than revenue: gross margin ranged from 17.0% (FY2021) to a peak of 36.5% (FY2023), a pattern consistent with a business whose main input costs (copper/aluminium, largely imported) can move independently of LKR selling prices during currency and commodity swings -- the FY2022/23 Annual Report notes the rupee fell 13% against the US dollar that year before FX liquidity improved in H2 (Annual Report 2022/23, p.108). The more durable story across the period is balance sheet deleveraging: total borrowings fell from a FY2022 peak of LKR 6.37Bn to LKR 1.39Bn by FY2025, while total equity more than doubled (LKR 15.28Bn to LKR 36.02Bn) on retained profit rather than new share capital (239,574,720 shares unchanged throughout). Dividend per share has been raised only twice in five years (LKR 0.75 -> 1.00 -> 1.25) and held flat since, a far more conservative payout trajectory than the swings in underlying profit would allow.
summary.gaps_note: This pass covers FY2021-FY2025 Group financial statements only, sourced directly from each year's own audited Statement of Profit or Loss, Statement of Financial Position, and Statement of Cash Flows (own-year figures, not later comparatives). Qualitative business narrative (Chairman's Statement, MD&A, segment detail) was not read in this pass -- causal explanations above are inferred from the numbers and risk-note disclosures only, not confirmed against management commentary. Company-only (non-consolidated) figures, quarterly/interim data, dividend history beyond DPS on the face of the income statement, and shareholder/segment detail are out of scope for this update.
summary.income_statement_analysis: Revenue grew from LKR 22.62Bn (FY2021) to LKR 37.49Bn (FY2025), a 66% increase over five years (13.4% CAGR), but the path was uneven: FY2022 revenue jumped 56% to LKR 35.33Bn, then fell in both FY2023 (-14.7%) and FY2024 (-3.2%) before rebounding 28.4% in FY2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Gross margin swung far more than revenue: 17.0% (FY2021) -> 22.5% (FY2022) -> 36.5% (FY2023) -> 24.5% (FY2024) -> 27.3% (FY2025), derived from gross profit/revenue each year. The FY2023 spike coincides with a year the FY2022/23 Annual Report's financial risk note flags as one where "the rupee fell by 13% against the US dollar" before FX liquidity improved in H2 (Annual Report 2022/23, p.108) -- consistent with a cable manufacturer whose main input (copper/aluminium, imported) can decouple sharply from LKR-denominated selling prices during currency and commodity swings, though this pass has not read the Chairman's/MD&A narrative pages to confirm the mechanism directly. Operating profit tracks the same pattern, rising from LKR 2.31Bn (FY2021) to a peak of LKR 9.08Bn (FY2023) before easing to LKR 7.47Bn (FY2025). Net finance income/(cost) flipped from a net cost in FY2021-FY2024 (as high as LKR -1.01Bn in FY2024) to a net income of LKR 444Mn in FY2025, mainly on a sharp fall in finance costs (LKR 1.01Bn to LKR 267Mn) rather than a rise in finance income, suggesting meaningful net debt paydown or refinancing at lower cost (see Balance Sheet tab). PAT is not proportional to PBT: profit attributable to non-controlling interests (NCI) has consistently taken 11-15% of Group PAT (e.g. LKR 840Mn of LKR 5.42Bn in FY2025), reflecting minority stakes in subsidiaries -- basic/diluted EPS (attributable to owners) was LKR 19.11 in FY2025 versus LKR 6.47 in FY2021, a 3x increase, roughly ahead of Group PAT growth (3.1x) itself since NCI's share of profit grew at a similar pace over the period.
summary.balance_sheet_analysis: Total assets grew from LKR 27.22Bn (FY2021) to LKR 43.65Bn (FY2025), +60%, while total equity grew faster: LKR 15.28Bn to LKR 36.02Bn, +136% -- meaning the balance sheet delevered materially over the period. This shows up directly in the liability mix: total liabilities actually fell in absolute terms, from LKR 11.94Bn (FY2021) to LKR 7.63Bn (FY2025), even as the balance sheet grew, cutting total liabilities from 44% of total assets (FY2021) to 17% (FY2025) (Statement of Financial Position, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Borrowings did almost all of the work: combined short- and long-term borrowings fell from LKR 3.85Bn (FY2021) to LKR 1.39Bn (FY2025), peaking at LKR 6.37Bn in FY2022 before declining every year since. Working capital composition shifted too -- inventory grew steadily and by far the most (LKR 7.90Bn to LKR 12.47Bn, +58%), consistent with the FY2022-23 currency/import-cost dynamics flagged on the Income Statement tab, while trade receivables were roughly flat to down (LKR 8.96Bn to LKR 7.32Bn, -18%) and trade payables swung sharply -- from LKR 6.55Bn (FY2021) down to LKR 900Mn (FY2023) and back up to LKR 2.13Bn (FY2025), a far bigger relative swing than any other single line, though the underlying supplier-mix reasons for this are not established here. Note: cash and cash equivalents are shown net of a reclassification -- the FY2025 Annual Report split what earlier years disclosed as a single "cash and cash equivalents" line into separate "cash and cash equivalents" and "short-term deposits" lines; the figures used here combine both for a consistent five-year series (LKR 2.53Bn FY2021 -> LKR 7.95Bn FY2025).
summary.cash_flow_analysis: Net cash from operating activities has been positive and comparatively stable across all five years (LKR 2.49Bn-3.93Bn), the only real outlier being FY2023 at the low end (LKR 2.56Bn) despite that year's peak profitability (see Income Statement tab) -- a sign that FY2023's unusually high margin did not convert one-for-one into operating cash that year, plausibly because of the working-capital swings noted on the Balance Sheet tab (Statement of Cash Flows, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Capex (purchases of property, plant & equipment plus capital work-in-progress) has been volatile and small relative to operating cash flow throughout: from a high of LKR 511Mn (FY2022) down to LKR 231Mn (FY2023) and back up to LKR 307Mn (FY2025) -- consistent with a business funding modest, steady capacity maintenance rather than an expansion phase. Financing activity is the more interesting story: FY2022 saw a net cash inflow from financing of LKR 2.03Bn (net new borrowing), but every year since has been a net outflow, growing to LKR -2.98Bn in FY2023 before easing to LKR -815Mn in FY2025 -- consistent with the sustained deleveraging seen on the Balance Sheet tab. Dividend payments by the Company itself have been flat in absolute LKR terms for three straight years (~LKR 299Mn in FY2023-2025 vs LKR 240Mn in FY2022 and LKR 180Mn in FY2021), i.e. dividend per share rose only twice (LKR 0.75 to 1.00 to 1.25) and has since been held constant rather than tracking the much larger swings in profit.
summary.equity_statement_analysis: Total equity attributable to owners of the company rose from LKR 13.33Bn (FY2021) to LKR 30.80Bn (FY2025), and NCI equity grew alongside it (LKR 1.95Bn to LKR 5.22Bn) roughly in step, so the ownership split of the Group's equity base has stayed fairly stable (NCI has consistently represented 13-15% of total equity across the period). Retained earnings is overwhelmingly the growth engine, rising from LKR 8.92Bn to LKR 25.55Bn (+186%) on retained profit, while stated capital has not changed at all (LKR 299,488k, 239,574,720 shares throughout) -- no new share issuance in the period; all equity growth is organic. The revaluation reserve jumped materially in FY2022 (to a running balance of LKR 2.97Bn, reaching LKR 3.52Bn by FY2025) following a land and buildings revaluation gain recognised that year (Statement of Changes in Equity, Annual Report 2021/22) and has been broadly stable since, with only small annual transfers to retained earnings (Statement of Changes in Equity, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Dividends paid to owners have been the main recurring equity outflow, rising from LKR 179.7Mn (FY2021) to LKR 299.5Mn (FY2023-2025), a far smaller claim on equity than the profit being retained each year -- consistent with a business reinvesting most of its earnings rather than distributing them.
summary.other_statements_analysis: Nothing unusual to add beyond the primary statements from this pass -- segment reporting, related-party transactions, and post-balance-sheet events were not separately reviewed for this five-year window. One item worth flagging for a future pass: the Group holds material equity-accounted investments (share of profit from associates, e.g. Resus Energy PLC) that contributed LKR 70-154Mn a year to profit before tax across the period (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports) -- a real but secondary earnings source that this analysis has not broken out from the four primary statements above.

PBT-tax-PAT identity holds for both bases. KEY OBSERVATION (not fabricated, derived from filing): Net finance income of Rs805.9mn (Group) is dominated by an exchange gain of Rs590.4mn (vs Rs117.2mn a year earlier), per Note 8 on p.9 ('Net Finance Income/(Cost) includes the exchange gains/losses'). This FX gain, not operating performance, is the primary driver of the 7.8% PBT growth despite operating profit falling 12.7% and gross margin compressing to 24.2% from 29.7% (gross profit Rs2,782,353 / revenue Rs11,486,953 vs Rs2,927,191/9,849,742), which we infer reflects rising input costs given cost of sales grew 25.7% vs revenue growth of 16.6% -- the filing does not include an MD&A/commentary section discussing copper/aluminium commodity prices explicitly, so this margin-compression driver is inferred from the reported cost-of-sales trend and the working-capital note (large Rs4,481,290 inventory build in the cash flow statement), not company-stated -- flagged as a gap.

thesis.thesis_text: ACL Cables PLC is an established Sri Lankan cable/wire manufacturer (Capital Goods) with five years of audited annual financials on file (FY2021-FY2025) plus a fresh Q1 FY2026/27 interim -- the best multi-period coverage in this batch. The interim quarter's headline numbers look strong (Group Revenue +16.6% YoY, PBT +7.8%, PAT +13.7% to Rs.2,128,135k), but this masks a real operating deterioration: Results from Operating Activities fell 12.7% YoY and gross margin compressed from 29.7% to 24.2% as Cost of Sales grew 25.7% against 16.6% revenue growth, consistent with rising copper/aluminium input costs. The entire PBT improvement, and then some, came from a Rs.473,190k YoY favourable swing in FX-driven net finance income (Note 8) -- not from cable-manufacturing profitability -- and should not be extrapolated forward. On a normalised basis (split-adjusted FY2025 EPS), the stock trades at ~14.8x trailing P/E and ~1.50x P/B -- fair rather than cheap once the FX effect is stripped out. The balance sheet remains strong (current ratio 5.31x) and export sales grew 33.0% YoY, a genuine positive, but the operating-profit decline and large working-capital-driven cash outflow (Rs.4,613,300k used this quarter) are the more durable signals than the FX-flattered PAT figure (Interim Financial Statements p.2, Note 8 p.9).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no copper/aluminium commodity-price or Sri Lanka cable-export data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence benefits from ACL's five-year annual history (FY2021-FY2025) plus this interim, giving a genuine multi-period trend unlike the other names in this batch, but is still capped by the FX-driven PAT quality issue this quarter (the entire PBT improvement came from a non-operating exchange gain, not operations) and by the filing's lack of an MD&A section discussing commodity-cost exposure explicitly.

financial_quality.rationale: ACL has genuine multi-year audited history on file (FY2021-FY2025 GROUP annuals plus this Q1 FY2026/27 interim), showing a strong balance sheet (current ratio 5.31x this quarter: current assets Rs.45,045,010k / current liabilities Rs.8,487,206k; total liabilities/equity just 0.24x) and equity growth from Rs.15,280,070k (FY2021) to Rs.36,020,087k (FY2025) to Rs.45,280,402k this quarter. However, annual PAT has been volatile -- Rs.1,753,722k (FY2021), Rs.5,113,980k (FY2022), a peak Rs.7,012,540k (FY2023), a drop to Rs.3,445,820k (FY2024), and Rs.5,419,537k (FY2025) -- not a smooth compounding trend. Most importantly, this quarter's PAT growth (+13.7% YoY to Rs.2,128,135k) is LOWER-QUALITY than it looks: Results from Operating Activities actually FELL 12.7% YoY and gross margin compressed ~550bps (29.7% to 24.2%) as Cost of Sales grew 25.7% against 16.6% revenue growth, consistent with rising copper/aluminium input costs (inferred from the cost trend and a Rs.4,481,290k inventory build, not company-stated). The entire PBT improvement (+7.8%) came from a Rs.473,190k favourable FX swing embedded in Net Finance Income (an FX gain of Rs.590,390k this quarter vs Rs.117,200k PY) -- a non-operating, currency-translation item that should not be extrapolated, and which masks the underlying operating deterioration.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue grew 16.6% YoY this quarter (Rs.9,849,742k to Rs.11,486,953k), with Export sales growing faster than Local (+33.0% to Rs.2,683,600k vs +12.4% to Rs.8,803,360k) -- a genuine positive diversification signal. But Results from Operating Activities fell 12.7% YoY, meaning revenue growth is not translating into operating profit growth this period. Over the five-year annual history, revenue has ranged narrowly (Rs.22.6bn FY2021 to Rs.37.5bn FY2025, non-linear: peaked Rs.35.3bn FY2022, dipped to Rs.29.2bn FY2024, before FY2025's rebound) rather than showing a clean compounding trend -- consistent with a cyclical, commodity-input-exposed cable manufacturer rather than a structurally high-growth business.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.94.30 (2026-08-28), naively annualising this quarter's EPS (Rs.2.56 x4 = Rs.10.24) implies a P/E of ~9.2x -- but this run-rate is inflated by the non-recurring FX gain identified above and should not be treated as sustainable earnings power. Using the FY2025 annual EPS of Rs.19.11, adjusted for the 3-for-1 share subdivision evident between the FY2025 annual (239,574,720 shares) and this interim (718,724,160 shares) -- i.e. ~Rs.6.37 split-adjusted -- gives a more conservative trailing P/E of ~14.8x. Book value of ~Rs.63.00/share (Group total equity Rs.45,280,402k / 718,724,160 shares) implies a P/B of ~1.50x, a middling multiple. Dividend history (FY2022-FY2024, pre-split, Rs.1.00-Rs.1.25) implies a modest split-adjusted yield of well under 1%. Overall valuation is fair rather than cheap once the FX-driven earnings-quality issue is accounted for.
citations: dividends: FY2024 DPS 1.25, FY2023 DPS 1.00, FY2022 DPS 1.00 (pre-split)

business_quality.rationale: ACL Cables is an established Sri Lankan cable/wire manufacturer (Capital Goods sector) with a five-year audited track record on file, a diversified segment mix (Manufacturing Cables 99.8% of external sales, plus smaller PVC Compound and Power/Energy segments), and a majority (51%) stake in CSLK (Cable Solutions PLC), also covered in this project -- a genuine strategic/vertical relationship. Export sales growing faster than Local (+33.0% vs +12.4% YoY) signals real market diversification. The business carries clear commodity-input exposure (copper/aluminium), evidenced by this quarter's margin compression, a structural, ongoing risk for the sector rather than a one-off.

governance_risk.rationale: ACL has a consistent five-year annual filing history plus timely interim filings on file, and cleanly executed a 3-for-1 share subdivision (239,574,720 to 718,724,160 shares) that is traceable across filings without discrepancy. No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify recent board/ownership changes. Disclosure has two filing-level gaps: no MD&A/commentary section discusses copper/aluminium commodity exposure explicitly (the margin-compression driver is inferred, not company-stated), and Note 8 discloses only a single net finance line with no gross income/cost split.

key_reasons: Five years of audited annual financials (FY2021-FY2025) plus a fresh interim quarter give a genuinely multi-period view -- among the best-covered names in this batch -- showing a strong balance sheet (current ratio 5.31x, total liabilities/equity 0.24x) but historically volatile annual PAT (Rs.1.75bn to a Rs.7.01bn peak to Rs.3.45bn to Rs.5.42bn over FY2021-2025)

This quarter's headline PAT growth (+13.7% YoY) is LOW QUALITY: Results from Operating Activities actually fell 12.7% and gross margin compressed ~550bps (29.7% to 24.2%) on rising input costs, while the entire PBT improvement came from a Rs.473,190k non-operating FX gain embedded in net finance income -- not a sign of improved cable-manufacturing profitability

Valuation is fair rather than cheap once the FX-driven earnings are normalised: ~14.8x trailing P/E on split-adjusted FY2025 EPS and ~1.50x P/B, versus a headline ~9.2x P/E that relies on non-recurring FX gains
watch_factors: The Rs.473,190k YoY favourable FX swing that drove all of this quarter's PBT growth is unlikely to repeat mechanically next quarter unless currency movements are similarly favourable -- the underlying operating decline (-12.7%) is the more durable signal

Gross margin compression (29.7% to 24.2%) alongside a large Rs.4,481,290k inventory build and a swing to a Rs.4,613,300k operating cash OUTFLOW (from a small inflow PY) is consistent with rising copper/aluminium costs and a deliberate inventory build -- worth monitoring for further margin pressure or a working-capital unwind

A 3-for-1 share subdivision occurred between the FY2025 annual filing and this interim (239,574,720 to 718,724,160 shares) -- confirmed consistent across filings, but worth flagging for anyone comparing pre- and post-split per-share figures

horizon_notes.6m: Next quarterly filing will show whether the FX-driven PBT boost reverses (if currency moves the other way) and whether the underlying operating-profit decline (-12.7%) continues or stabilises.
horizon_notes.1y: If gross margin stays compressed near 24% versus the ~30% historically seen, FY2026/27 full-year operating profit could fall short of FY2025's Rs.7,466,034k despite revenue growth -- worth tracking against the five-year annual base already on file.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on ACL's ability to pass through copper/aluminium cost inflation via pricing without losing export competitiveness (exports grew 33.0% YoY this quarter, a positive sign).
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year global copper/aluminium commodity cycle or Sri Lanka's cable-export competitiveness.

interim_updates.note_text: ACL Cables PLC (ACL) reported Group Revenue of Rs.11,486.95mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 16.6% YoY from Rs.9,849.74mn, but Group operating performance actually deteriorated: Results from Operating Activities fell 12.7% YoY to Rs.1,939.32mn (2025: Rs.2,220.20mn), and Group Gross Profit Margin compressed to 24.2% from 29.7% (Gross Profit Rs.2,782.35mn / Revenue Rs.11,486.95mn vs Rs.2,927.19mn / Rs.9,849.74mn PY) as Cost of Sales grew 25.7% YoY (Rs.8,704.60mn vs Rs.6,922.55mn), well ahead of the 16.6% revenue growth. By business segment (Note 1(a), p.8): the core Manufacturing Cables segment generated external sales of Rs.11,464.88mn (99.8% of Group external revenue) with segment profit before other income and finance cost of Rs.1,586.68mn; the smaller Manufacturing PVC Compound segment contributed Rs.245.68mn and Others (Power and Energy) Rs.88.93mn, against a combined-segment total of Rs.1,921.40mn PBIT (down from Rs.2,198.14mn PY, -12.6%, consistent with the Group-level operating profit decline). Geographically, Export sales grew faster than Local: Group export sales +33.0% YoY to Rs.2,683.60mn (2025: Rs.2,017.07mn) vs Local sales +12.4% YoY to Rs.8,803.36mn (2025: Rs.7,832.67mn) (Note 1(b)). Despite the operating-profit decline, Group Profit Before Tax grew 7.8% YoY to Rs.2,757.57mn (2025: Rs.2,557.33mn) -- entirely because Net Finance Income surged to Rs.805.87mn from Rs.302.44mn PY (+166.5%), which per Note 8 (p.9) was DOMINATED by a foreign exchange gain of Rs.590.39mn this quarter versus just Rs.117.20mn a year earlier (a Rs.473.19mn favourable FX swing) -- not an improvement in underlying operations. Income Tax Expense fell 8.3% YoY to Rs.629.44mn (2025: Rs.686.10mn), and Profit for the Period rose 13.7% YoY to Rs.2,128.14mn (2025: Rs.1,871.24mn), with EPS up to Rs.2.56 from Rs.2.24. At the Company (parent, standalone) level the same pattern holds but is more pronounced: Company revenue +12.1% YoY to Rs.5,634.18mn, Company operating profit +8.6% YoY to Rs.1,005.99mn (a smaller decline than at Group level since PVC-compound/Others margin pressure sits mostly in subsidiaries), Company PBT +18.4% YoY to Rs.1,176.74mn on a Company-level net finance income of Rs.170.75mn (2025: Rs.67.49mn, +153.0%) that included an exchange gain of Rs.173.55mn (2025: Rs.50.11mn). The cash flow statement shows a large working-capital drag behind the P&L strength: Group Inventories grew by Rs.4,481.29mn during the quarter, pulling Net Cash Used in Operating Activities to Rs.(4,613.30)mn (2025: Rs.+66.43mn generated) -- a swing of over Rs.4.68bn, funded largely by a Rs.1,891.39mn net increase in short-term borrowings and a Rs.2,558.80mn net cash inflow from investing activities (mostly realisation of Rs.2,550.00mn of Financial Assets at FVTPL).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is ACL's first interim_updates entry in this DB. The only prior row in financial_statements for ACL was an ANNUAL row for FY2025 (year ended 31 March 2025) -- this is EXPLICITLY noted as NOT a usable interim predecessor (different period length and period type), so only YoY (vs the filing's own 3-months-ended-30-June-2025 comparative column) is computed. Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the filing does not include an MD&A/commentary section discussing copper/aluminium commodity prices explicitly, despite ACL being a cable manufacturer with clear input-commodity exposure -- the 25.7% cost-of-sales growth against 16.6% revenue growth (margin compression 29.7% to 24.2%) is inferred to reflect rising input costs from the reported trend and the large Rs.4,481.29mn inventory build in the cash flow statement, but this is inference, not company-stated fact; (2) Note 8 discloses only the net exchange gain/loss embedded within 'Net Finance Income/(Cost)', not a full gross finance income/finance cost split -- the filing presents only ONE net finance line throughout, so finance_costs is stored as 0 and finance_income holds the net figure, a presentation choice of the source filing, not a data-entry gap; (3) the FY2026 vs FY2025 segment comparison for Manufacturing PVC Compound and Others (Power and Energy) is only available at the PBIT level for the current quarter split by segment -- the PY column in Note 1(a) gives only a Group TOTAL (Rs.2,198.14mn), not a PY segment-by-segment breakdown, so which specific segment drove the operating-profit decline cannot be isolated beyond the dominant Manufacturing Cables segment's implied share.
interim_updates.takeaway: ACL's headline PBT and PAT growth (+7.8% and +13.7% YoY) mask a genuine operating deterioration: Results from Operating Activities fell 12.7% and gross margin compressed by roughly 550bps (29.7% to 24.2%) as cost of sales outgrew revenue. The entire PBT improvement, and then some, came from a Rs.473.19mn favourable swing in foreign-exchange-driven net finance income (Note 8) -- a non-operating, currency-translation item rather than a sign of improved cable-manufacturing profitability. The 25.7% cost-of-sales growth alongside a large working-capital-driven cash outflow (inventories +Rs.4,481.29mn, operating cash flow swinging to a Rs.4,613.30mn outflow) is consistent with rising copper/aluminium input costs and a deliberate inventory build, though the filing itself does not discuss commodity prices directly. Investors should treat the FX-driven PBT/PAT beat as unlikely to repeat mechanically next quarter unless the currency moves similarly again.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.11,486.95mn, +16.6% YoY (2025: Rs.9,849.74mn); Results from Operating Activities Rs.1,939.32mn, -12.7% YoY; PBT Rs.2,757.57mn, +7.8% YoY; PAT Rs.2,128.14mn, +13.7% YoY; EPS Rs.2.56 (2025: Rs.2.24).
Group gross margin compressed to 24.2% from 29.7% PY as Cost of Sales grew 25.7% YoY against 16.6% revenue growth.

Net Finance Income surged to Rs.805.87mn from Rs.302.44mn PY (+166.5%), dominated by an FX gain of Rs.590.39mn (2025: Rs.117.20mn) per Note 8 -- this, not operations, is the primary driver of PBT growth.
Export sales grew 33.0% YoY to Rs.2,683.60mn, outpacing Local sales growth of 12.4% to Rs.8,803.36mn.
Company (standalone) PBT +18.4% YoY to Rs.1,176.74mn on a Company-level exchange gain of Rs.173.55mn (2025: Rs.50.11mn).
Net Cash Used in Operating Activities was Rs.(4,613.30)mn (2025: Rs.+66.43mn), a Rs.4.68bn swing driven by a Rs.4,481.29mn inventory build.
key_drivers: FX gain of Rs.590.39mn embedded in Net Finance Income (vs Rs.117.20mn PY, a Rs.473.19mn favourable swing) is the primary driver of the 7.8% Group PBT growth, masking a 12.7% decline in operating profit.
Gross margin compression from 29.7% to 24.2% (Cost of Sales +25.7% vs Revenue +16.6%) reflects rising input costs, inferred from the cost trend and a large inventory build, not company-stated.
Export sales growth of 33.0% YoY outpaced Local sales growth of 12.4%, shifting the Group's revenue mix toward exports.

compare_snapshot.summary_text: ACL Cables manufactures and sells electrical cables and related products in Sri Lanka through its own operations and several subsidiaries/associates (including Kelani Cables PLC and Resus Energy PLC) (Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, Annual Report 2024/25). Group revenue rose from LKR 22.62Bn (FY2021) to LKR 37.49Bn (FY2025), +66% over five years, but not steadily -- it spiked 56% in FY2022, then fell for two straight years before rebounding sharply in FY2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Profitability has been considerably more volatile than revenue: gross margin ranged from 17.0% (FY2021) to a peak of 36.5% (FY2023), a pattern consistent with a business whose main input costs (copper/aluminium, largely imported) can move independently of LKR selling prices during currency and commodity swings -- the FY2022/23 Annual Report notes the rupee fell 13% against the US dollar that year before FX liquidity improved in H2 (Annual Report 2022/23, p.108). The more durable story across the period is balance sheet deleveraging: total borrowings fell from a FY2022 peak of LKR 6.37Bn to LKR 1.39Bn by FY2025, while total equity more than doubled (LKR 15.28Bn to LKR 36.02Bn) on retained profit rather than new share capital (239,574,720 shares unchanged throughout). Dividend per share has been raised only twice in five years (LKR 0.75 -> 1.00 -> 1.25) and held flat since, a far more conservative payout trajectory than the swings in underlying profit would allow.
compare_snapshot.gaps_note: This pass covers FY2021-FY2025 Group financial statements only, sourced directly from each year's own audited Statement of Profit or Loss, Statement of Financial Position, and Statement of Cash Flows (own-year figures, not later comparatives). Qualitative business narrative (Chairman's Statement, MD&A, segment detail) was not read in this pass -- causal explanations above are inferred from the numbers and risk-note disclosures only, not confirmed against management commentary. Company-only (non-consolidated) figures, quarterly/interim data, dividend history beyond DPS on the face of the income statement, and shareholder/segment detail are out of scope for this update.

thesis.thesis_text: ACL Cables PLC is an established Sri Lankan cable/wire manufacturer (Capital Goods) with five years of audited annual financials on file (FY2021-FY2025) plus a fresh Q1 FY2026/27 interim -- the best multi-period coverage in this batch. The interim quarter's headline numbers look strong (Group Revenue +16.6% YoY, PBT +7.8%, PAT +13.7% to Rs.2,128,135k), but this masks a real operating deterioration: Results from Operating Activities fell 12.7% YoY and gross margin compressed from 29.7% to 24.2% as Cost of Sales grew 25.7% against 16.6% revenue growth, consistent with rising copper/aluminium input costs. The entire PBT improvement, and then some, came from a Rs.473,190k YoY favourable swing in FX-driven net finance income (Note 8) -- not from cable-manufacturing profitability -- and should not be extrapolated forward. On a normalised basis (split-adjusted FY2025 EPS), the stock trades at ~14.8x trailing P/E and ~1.50x P/B -- fair rather than cheap once the FX effect is stripped out. The balance sheet remains strong (current ratio 5.31x) and export sales grew 33.0% YoY, a genuine positive, but the operating-profit decline and large working-capital-driven cash outflow (Rs.4,613,300k used this quarter) are the more durable signals than the FX-flattered PAT figure (Interim Financial Statements p.2, Note 8 p.9).
